name: Peleg
title: He in whose days the earth was divided
summary: Peleg was a descendant of Shem, son of Noah's son, and father of Reu in the lineage from Shem to Abraham. His name means "division," and he is known for the earth being divided in his days, which is traditionally linked to the confusion of languages at Babel and the scattering of peoples across the earth. He is an important link in the patriarchal line from Noah to Abraham.

keyEvents.title: The Birth of Peleg and the Division of the Earth
keyEvents.description: Peleg was born as the son of Eber, and in his days the earth was divided. His name was given as a reminder of this great event.

keyEvents.title: Peleg's Place in the Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Peleg is mentioned in the genealogy in Genesis 10 as part of Shem's lineage, and his brother Joktan became the ancestor of many Arab peoples.

keyEvents.title: Peleg's Lineage from Shem to Abraham
keyEvents.description: In Shem's family tree, Peleg is noted as an important link in the line from Shem through Eber to Abraham. He was 30 years old when he had his son Reu.

keyEvents.title: Peleg's Lifespan
keyEvents.description: According to Genesis, Peleg lived for 239 years. After having Reu, he lived another 209 years and had more sons and daughters.

keyEvents.title: Peleg in Luke's Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Peleg is mentioned in Jesus' genealogy in the Gospel of Luke, confirming his place in the messianic line from Adam through Abraham and David to Jesus Christ.

keyEvents.title: Peleg in the Genealogies of Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Peleg is mentioned in 1 Chronicles as part of the great genealogy that begins with Adam and continues through Shem's line to the patriarchs of Israel.
